catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Ударение силовое (экспираторное). Фиксировано в большинстве случаев на определенном слоге. В случаях, когда слово равно основе, ударение падает на второй слог: адá 'отец', дидé 'мать', хилáб 'лошадь', къапý 'дверь', джидáр 'путы', серми́сагъ 'чеснок' и др. В других случаях ударение может падать на первый, третий и другие слоги слова: чагъáр 'идти' – чáгъари (наст. общее вр.), къечIи́ 'подняться' > къéчIира (буд.вр.), джургIáм 'отвага' > джургIамлý 'отважный' и т.д. Ударение может иметь слово- и форморазличительную функцию, так, оно отличает форму настоящего времени от долженствовательной формы глагола: наст. вр. чáгъари и долж. ф. чагъáри от чагъáр 'идти'; наст. вр. и́рхъири и долж. ф. ирхъи́ри от ирхъи́ 'смотреть' и т.д.

sweep_summary: Budukh (budu1248) is not in the catalog. The single works with stress in the title, Authier 2010 'Finite and non-finite: Prosodic distinctions on Budugh verb stems' (Benjamins SLCS 121, pp. 143-164, DOI 10.1075/slcs.121.05aut), is about word prosody of this language: its publisher abstract (saved as Crossref record, says the dependent/independent distinction of verb stems is prosodic, dependent stems taking noun prosody and independent ones finite-verb prosody, but gives no syllable placement and does not say stress vs. tone. Full text is closed everywhere probed (OpenAlex/S2 closed, no HAL file, Benjamins/Google Books/academia/ResearchGate could not be reached by automated download, nothing on archive.org/OAPEN/HathiTrust); priority high, it is the likely arbiter for this language. Metadata-only extras seen: Authier 2026 Word Structure 19(2-3):152-173 (DOI 10.3366/word.2026.0267, verb-stem morphology, closed) and Authier 2013 Faits de Langues 41 (possession, closed). 2.1.2 pp. 446-447: dynamic stress, on the 2nd syllable when word = stem (adá, didé, q'apú), other syllables in inflected/derived forms, contrastive present čáǧari vs debitive čaǧári; contradicted by Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990 p. 346 item 4: 'Словесное ударение отсутствует' (no word stress; syllable tone, phrase accent by tone and syllable weight). in the budu1248 our files updated with a stamped pass-2 block.org APIs and direct downloads.

new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress is dynamic (expiratory). In most cases it is fixed on a particular syllable. When the word equals the stem, stress falls on the second syllable: adá 'father', didé 'mother', ... q'apú 'door', džidár 'hobble', sermísaǧ 'garlic', etc. In other cases stress may fall on the first, third and other syllables of the word: čaǧár 'to go' – čáǧari (general present), q'eč'í 'to rise' > q'éč'ira (future), džurʕám 'courage' > džurʕamlú 'brave', etc. Stress can distinguish words and forms; thus it distinguishes the present tense from the debitive form of the verb: pres. čáǧari vs deb. čaǧári from čaǧár 'go'; pres. írqiri vs deb. irqíri from irqí 'look', etc.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Dynamic stress, largely fixed: in uninflected words (word = stem) it sits on the second syllable; in inflected and derived forms its position is morphologically determined (e.g. initial in the general present, second in the debitive, on the suffix in -lu adjectives), so stress placement can distinguish grammatical forms.
new_statements.exceptions: Inflected/derived forms depart from the second-syllable pattern (present čáǧari initial; debitive čaǧári; future q'éč'ira initial; adjectival džurʕamlú final). NB a competing first-hand description held by the project, Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990: 346, states 'Словесное ударение отсутствует' (no word stress; syllable tone, phrase accent governed by tones and syllable weight).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms; 'word = stem' (bare stem nouns/verbs) vs affixed forms. One three-syllable stem example (sermísaǧ) shows second rather than final syllable. Kodzasov 1990 instead treats prominence as phrase-level accent over lexical syllable tones; Authier 2010 (abstract) confirms that prosodic patterns differ systematically between nominal/dependent and finite verb forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Both quoted sources describe the language of Buduq (Budukh) village, Quba district, Azerbaijan = budu1248; Šejxov states the language has no dialects. Authier spells it 'Budugh'.

new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress is dynamic (expiratory). In most cases it is fixed on a particular syllable. When the word equals the stem, stress falls on the second syllable: adá 'father', didé 'mother', xiláb 'horse', q'apú 'door', džidár 'hobbles', sermísaǧ 'garlic', etc. In other cases stress may fall on the first, third and other syllables of the word: čaǧár 'to go' – čáǧari (general present), q'ečIú 'to climb' > q'éčIira (future), džurgIát 'courage' > džurgIatlú 'brave', etc. Stress can have a word- and form-distinguishing function [p.447: present čáǧari vs debitive čaǧári from čaǧár 'go'; present írq'iri vs debitive irq'íri from irq'ír 'look'].
new_statements.citation: Šejxov, E. M. 2001 [1st ed. 1999]. Buduxskij jazyk. In M. E. Alekseev (ed.), Jazyki mira: Kavkazskie jazyki, 445-452. Moskva: Academia. Sec. 2.1.2, pp. 446-447

new_statements.reading: Dynamic word stress, described as fixed in most cases: on the second syllable of uninflected stems (bare stems = words), with stress moving to first/third/other syllables in inflected and derived forms, and lexically/morphologically contrastive placement (present vs. debitive). This is the only source read that states a stress-placement rule. It is directly contradicted by the phonetician's first-hand fieldwork statement in Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990, Sopostavitel'noe izuchenie dagestanskix jazykov: Imja. Fonetika, sec. 20, p. Место фразового акцента в слове, очевидно, предопределено распределением тонов и "тяжестью" слогов.' ('Word stress is absent. The place of the phrase accent within the word is evidently predetermined by the distribution of tones and the "weight" of syllables'), with preliminary syllable-tone marks (R/F/L/H) in item 3. Authier 2010 (unread, abstract only) reports a word-prosodic contrast between noun-type and finite-verb-type patterns, which is compatible with Šejxov's form-distinguishing accent shifts but does not settle stress vs. tone. Any catalog entry should code Šejxov's 2nd-stem-syllable dynamic stress as the placement statement with an explicit 'contested: K&K 1990 report no word stress / syllable tone; Authier 2010 pending' flag.

sources.quote: In Budugh, a small Daghestanian language spoken in Azerbaijan, verb-stems, defined as verb forms uninflected for tense or mood, can be used either as dependent of nouns ('participles') and other predicates ... or as finite non-indicative verb forms ... The main distinction between dependent and independent uses is prosodic: dependent verb forms adopt the prosodic features of nouns, while the same forms, if syntactically independent, share the same prosodic pattern as other indicative or more complex modal forms which are segmentally marked (suffixed) as such.
sources.locator: publisher abstract (Crossref record, jats:p); chapter pp. 143-164 not opened
sources.note: Only modern fieldwork-based treatment of Budugh word prosody (noun vs finite-verb accent patterns); abstract confirms prosodic contrasts but the stress rule itself is in the unread body.
